description:
The image displays two concentric pie charts comparing the distribution of categories across two different datasets or classification systems — one labeled implicitly on the left (possibly a baseline or source dataset) and the other explicitly titled “FineWeb-Edu Classifier” on the right. Both charts are segmented into hierarchical categories, with outer rings representing broader domains (e.g., Education, Science, Health & Medicine) and inner rings breaking these down into more specific subcategories (e.g., Teaching & resources, Historical review, Diseases).

In the left chart, the largest segment is “Education” (25), followed by “Health & Medicine” (22), “Science” (15), and “History & Society” (23). Subcategories under “Education” include “Teaching & resources” (15) and “Science & technology education” (10). Under “Health & Medicine,” we see “Diseases” (11), “Nutrition” (5), and “Medical” (6). “Science” breaks into “Animal & Plant” (13) and “Materials” (2). “History & Society” includes “Historical review” (7), “Society & culture” (10), and “Events & people” (6). The smallest segments are in the “Tech & Engineer” group: “Infor tech” (5), “Materials” (3), “Emerging tech” (4), “Manage” (2), and “Policy” (1), along with “Fin & Law” (3).

The right chart, “FineWeb-Edu Classifier,” shows a similar structure but with different proportions. “Education” is now the largest segment (38), with “Teaching & resources” (17) and “Science & technology education” (19) as its main subcategories. “Health & Medicine” is 19, broken into “Diseases” (10), “Nutrition” (7), and “Medical” (2). “Science” is 15, with “Animal & Plant” (12) and “Materials” (3). “History & Society” is 19, including “Historical review” (12) and “Society & culture” (5). Smaller segments include “Events & people” (2), “Infor tech” (3), “Emerging tech” (4), “Materials” (1), “Manage” (1), and “Healthy education” (2). The “Tech & Engineer” category is partially visible and appears to be very small.

The visual comparison suggests that the FineWeb-Edu Classifier places greater emphasis on educational content, particularly “Teaching & resources” and “Science & technology education,” while reducing the relative size of technical and policy-related categories. The charts use color-coding to distinguish domains (green for Education, blue for Health & Medicine, red for Science, orange for History & Society, and brown for Tech & Engineer), with labels and numerical values inside each segment. The inner rings are slightly offset (exploded) for clarity, and lines connect small segments to their labels. This visualization likely illustrates how a data selection or classification model (possibly using attention mechanisms, as suggested by the paper title) reshapes the distribution of educational content by prioritizing certain domains over others.
